sources.entry: Aimeos - E-commerce framework for building custom online shops, market places and complex B2B applications scaling to billions of items with Laravel. (Demo, Source Code) LGPL-3.0/MIT PHP

summary.one_liner: Aimeos is a Laravel-based e-commerce platform and framework for building online shops, multi-vendor marketplaces and B2B applications.
summary.what_it_does: Aimeos is a PHP e-commerce package that can be installed as a standalone shop distribution via Composer or added to an existing Laravel application. It provides a JSON REST API and a GraphQL API for administration, plus an admin backend at /admin and a frontend shop. The README lists support for bundles, vouchers, subscriptions with recurring payments, block/tier pricing, and multi-vendor, multi-channel and multi-warehouse setups. It also describes an MCP server that lets AI agents manage products, categories, customers and orders, authenticated with Sanctum tokens or optionally Laravel Passport OAuth. Optional settings enable multi-language routing, top-level multi-routing for category and product URLs, and vendor self-registration.
use_cases: build an online shop with Laravel
add e-commerce to an existing Laravel site
build a headless shop for a SPA or PWA
manage shop products and orders via AI agents
how_to_run: wget -O composer https://getcomposer.org/composer.phar (download Composer; URL not given in README, see note)
notable: Headless distribution with API-only and JWT authentication pre-configured for SPA/PWA builds
MCP server for AI agents (Claude, ChatGPT) to manage shop data
Multi-vendor, multi-shop mode with optional seller self-registration
Subscriptions with recurring payments and 100+ payment gateways (per README)
Full RTL support in frontend and backend
caveats: Multi-routing adds extra database queries per request and affects performance, per the README
Requires PHP 8.2+ and a supported SQL database; hosting needs the document root set to the public/ directory
Extending MCP OAuth login requires installing Laravel Passport separately
